newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends mid-range after lacklustre day.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends mid-range after lacklustre day.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended around mid-range on Wednesday after a lacklustre day's trading that saw the market fluctuate either side of $200 a tonne, brokers said.

They said business remained nervous and directionless after dipping in early trade on U.S. stocks data showing year-ago stock levels for U.S. distillates had moved into surplus for the first time since June 1995.
Feb gas oil ended $2 down at $201, around the middle of a $5.50 trading range.

The Feb/March backwardation, the focus of attention for both spot and futures traders because of a perceived squeeze by one U.S. trade house, narrowed slightly to around $7.50 after stretching out to $10 on Tuesday.

Traders said there was some evidence of position rolling that took some of the pressure off the Feb contract but they said there was still plenty of time for the spread to widen out again ahead of the Feb contract expiry on February 12.

Dealers said NYMEX heating oil was still very much in the driving seat as far as direction was concerned with ample supplies, lack of arbitrage opportunities and above normal temperatures in much of Europe keeping sentiment weak.
"You have to look at the products in the States to get a lead from them for the moment because volume is incredibly thin here (London)," one trader.
March Brent was trading six cents higher at $22.49 a barrel.
